label: IX.8, 1049b4–1050b6 — Three comparisons of actuality and capacity in Aristotle Θ.8
interpretation: Priority in account concerns the corresponding activity to which the account of a capacity refers. Priority in substance is argued from mature form and actuality as end. The temporal argument makes two comparisons: the seed precedes the mature individual, and an actual individual of the same kind, numerically different, precedes the seed itself (τούτων πρότερα τῷ χρόνῳ). The individual’s capacity can precede its own exercise.
attribution: The passage states that actuality is prior in account and in substance, and that in time the seed precedes this mature human while another actual human, the same in kind and different in number, precedes the seed; more generally, in the generation under discussion, what is potential comes to actuality through something already actual, although the individual’s own capacity can precede its exercise, which is the premise.
